evals.name: node-project-full-setup
evals.prompt: Set up the pipeline for this task: Add a rate limiter middleware to the Express API that limits each IP to 100 requests per 15-minute window.
evals.expected_output: Worktree created, commands read from orchestrate.config.json, baseline metrics recorded in .harness/add-rate-limiter-middleware/baseline.json, all environment variables returned
expectations: Invokes the using-git-worktrees skill via the Skill tool to create a worktree
Stores and reports WORKTREE_PATH as an absolute path
Stores and reports BRANCH_NAME for the worktree branch
Reads orchestrate.config.json from the repo root to get the commands to run
Runs the typecheck, lint, and test commands the config names and records their exit codes
Records null for any metric whose command the config does not name, rather than failing
Creates .harness/<SPEC_NAME>/ directory with a slugified spec name derived from the task
Writes baseline.json with type_check, lint, test, coverage, and timestamp keys
Returns all five output variables: WORKTREE_PATH, BRANCH_NAME, SPEC_NAME, SPEC_DIR, BASELINE_PATH
anti_expectations: Does not skip creating a git worktree and work directly on the main branch
Does not walk package.json, pyproject.toml, or any manifest to discover which commands to run
Does not write a commands block into baseline.json
Does not guess a file-filter flag or classify the test runner itself

evals.name: python-project-baseline-metrics
evals.prompt: Set up the pipeline environment for: Refactor the database connection pool to support async connections with configurable pool size.
evals.expected_output: Worktree created, commands taken from orchestrate.config.json, baseline metrics captured from those commands, spec directory created at .harness/refactor-db-connection-pool/
expectations: Invokes the using-git-worktrees skill to create an isolated worktree
Changes directory into the worktree after creation
Reads orchestrate.config.json rather than inspecting the project to identify it as Python
Runs the typecheck command the config names and records exit code and error count
Runs the lint command the config names and records exit code and warning count
Runs the test command the config names and records passed, failed, and skipped counts
Captures coverage percentage from the coverage command the config names, when it names one
Derives a slugified SPEC_NAME from the task description (e.g., refactor-db-connection-pool)
Writes baseline.json with a timestamp field in ISO format
anti_expectations: Does not infer the toolchain from pyproject.toml, setup.py, or any other manifest
Does not substitute a default command such as mypy or pytest when the config names a different one
Does not create the spec directory before the worktree is set up

evals.name: partial-config-graceful-handling
evals.prompt: Set up pipeline for: Add a webhook endpoint that validates GitHub signatures and forwards events to our internal queue.
evals.expected_output: Worktree created, only the commands the config names are run, baseline.json written with null entries for the rest, all output variables populated
expectations: Announces 'Setting up pipeline environment.' at the start
Invokes using-git-worktrees skill before any other operations
Records null for type_check, lint, test, or coverage keys when the config names no command for them
Does not fail or exit early when the config names commands for only some of the four tools
Creates the .harness/ directory structure even when the config is partial
Baseline.json contains all required keys (type_check, lint, test, coverage, timestamp) regardless of which commands the config named
Returns SPEC_DIR as the path to .harness/<SPEC_NAME>/
anti_expectations: Does not abort when the config omits a command for one of the four tools
Does not omit keys from baseline.json instead of recording null
Does not fall back to detecting a command the config left out

evals.name: stale-config-halts-as-config-error
evals.prompt: Set up the pipeline for: Tighten the input validation on the signup endpoint.
evals.expected_output: Stage 0 halts naming the command that did not resolve and says the config needs updating; no baseline.json recording it as a failing suite
expectations: Reads orchestrate.config.json and runs the commands it names
Detects that 'npm run typecheck:strict' does not resolve — the script does not exist
Halts rather than continuing, and names the command that failed to resolve
States that orchestrate.config.json is stale and needs updating
Distinguishes a shell-level failure (missing script, exit 127) from a suite that ran and came back red
anti_expectations: Does not record the unresolved command as type_check with a non-zero exit in baseline.json
Does not silently skip the command and continue with a partial baseline
Does not fall back to detecting a replacement typecheck command

evals.name: missing-config-halts
evals.prompt: Set up the pipeline for: Add pagination to the orders list endpoint.
evals.expected_output: Halts because orchestrate.config.json does not exist, and tells the user to run setup-harness
expectations: Looks for orchestrate.config.json at the repo root
Halts when the file does not exist
Names setup-harness as the skill that writes the file
anti_expectations: Does not fall back to auto-detecting commands from package.json or any other manifest
Does not write a baseline.json with all-null metrics and continue
Does not author orchestrate.config.json itself as part of this run
